Instead of allocating contiguous VRAM blocks for the maximum possible sequence length (which wastes 60-80% of VRAM due to internal and external fragmentation), PagedAttention partitions KV tensors into fixed-size physical memory pages, dynamically mapping logical sequence tokens to non-contiguous GPU pages.

doc_sys_020.title: Quantization Basics: INT8 vs FP8 Formats
doc_sys_020.text: Post-training quantization and quantized fine-tuning compress FP16 model weights into 8-bit representations. INT8 represents values as signed 8-bit integers using scale and zero-point parameters. Modern FP8 formats (E4M3 for weights/activations and E5M2 for gradients) maintain floating-point dynamic range, allowing hardware acceleration directly on Ada Lovelace and Hopper Tensor Cores.

doc_sys_021.title: Weight-Only Quantization (W8A16 / W4A16)
doc_sys_021.text: In memory-bandwidth-bound LLM text generation with batch size 1, weight-only quantization stores model parameters in INT8 or INT4 while keeping activations in FP16. Before matrix multiplication, weights are dequantized on-the-fly to FP16 in registers, cutting memory bandwidth traffic across GPU HBM by 50% to 75%.

doc_sys_022.title: Speculative Decoding Acceleration Overview
doc_sys_022.text: Speculative decoding pairs a small, fast draft model with a large target model. The draft model quickly proposes K candidate tokens autoregressively. The target model evaluates all K proposed tokens simultaneously in a single parallel forward pass, accepting candidates that match its probability distribution and rejecting deviations, delivering 2x-3x latency reductions without changing output quality.

doc_sys_023.title: Activation Memory vs Parameter Memory Scaling with Context Length
doc_sys_023.text: While model parameter memory remains strictly constant regardless of input size, activation memory scales linearly with sequence length in modern tiled attention, and quadratically in standard attention. At sequence lengths of 8k or 32k tokens, activation memory easily surpasses model weight memory, necessitating gradient checkpointing and FlashAttention.

doc_sys_024.title: Python Garbage Collector Generation Thresholds
doc_sys_024.text: CPython manages cyclic garbage collection using three generational pools (Generation 0, 1, and 2). gc.set_threshold(threshold0, threshold1, threshold2) controls the frequency of garbage collection cycles. During training loops, cyclic GC pauses can cause periodic latency stuttering; tuning thresholds or disabling GC during timed iterations stabilizes step times.

doc_sys_025.title: PyTorch Distributed RPC Framework
doc_sys_025.text: PyTorch's Remote Procedure Call (RPC) framework allows running functions remotely across distributed cluster nodes. It provides rpc_sync, rpc_async, and remote reference (RRef) mechanisms, serving as the foundational infrastructure for parameter server architectures and pipeline parallelism (PiPPy).

doc_sys_val_001.title: Verifying Free-Threaded Python Support in C Extensions
doc_sys_val_001.text: In Python 3.13 free-threaded builds, C extensions must explicitly declare support for running without the GIL using PyUnstable_Module_SetGIL(mod, Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED). If an imported C extension does not declare compatibility, the Python runtime automatically re-enables the GIL for the entire process to prevent memory corruption.

doc_sys_val_002.title: FlashAttention Head Dimension Alignment Constraints
doc_sys_val_002.text: FlashAttention imposes specific hardware alignment requirements: the head dimension (head_dim) must be a multiple of 8 (and typically <= 256), inputs must be contiguous in memory, and data types must be Float16 or BFloat16 on NVIDIA Ampere (SM 80+) or newer architectures. If these constraints are violated, SDPA falls back to the Math or Efficient backend.

doc_sys_val_003.title: LoRA Adapter Swapping in Multi-Tenant Serving
doc_sys_val_003.text: Because LoRA parameters represent only a tiny fraction of total model weights, serving engines can host a single shared copy of frozen base model weights in GPU VRAM and dynamically swap small LoRA adapter matrices (A and B) per request, enabling multi-tenant personalized model serving without loading separate 7B+ model instances.

doc_sys_val_004.title: Sliding Window Attention (Local Attention) Memory Ceiling
doc_sys_val_004.text: Sliding Window Attention restricts each token to attending only to a local window of W preceding tokens. In autoregressive generation, this caps the active KV cache size per sequence to exactly W tokens rather than growing unbounded to the full sequence length, maintaining constant VRAM consumption for infinitely long text streams.

doc_sys_val_005.title: Context Manager for Profiling Host vs GPU Time: record_function
doc_sys_val_005.text: torch.autograd.profiler.record_function(name) is a context manager that labels custom user code blocks inside the PyTorch Profiler and Chrome Trace timeline. It enables attributing CPU host overhead and downstream CUDA kernel launches to specific high-level PyTorch modules or functions.

doc_sys_test_001.title: Why Python Free-Threaded Builds Re-Enable the GIL Automatically
doc_sys_test_001.text: If a Python 3.13 script starts with the GIL disabled, but subsequently imports an older C extension library that has not been compiled with Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED, the CPython interpreter will print a warning and immediately re-lock the GIL for all threads to ensure thread-safety against legacy global state.

doc_sys_test_002.title: Diagnosing Silent Fallbacks to SDPA Math Backend
doc_sys_test_002.text: When SDPA silently falls back from FlashAttention to the slow Math backend, it is typically caused by passing non-contiguous query/key tensors, using Float32 precision instead of FP16/BF16, or providing custom non-standard attention bias shapes. Disabling the math backend via sdpa_kernel(enable_math=False) forces PyTorch to raise an informative error detailing the exact constraint violation.

doc_sys_test_003.title: Preventing Dynamic KV Cache GPU Memory Fragmentation
doc_sys_test_003.text: Repeatedly calling torch.cat on KV cache tensors at every generated token causes frequent reallocation of growing buffers. This rapid churn of varying tensor sizes creates severe virtual memory fragmentation in PyTorch's caching allocator. Switching to a pre-allocated static cache with slice assignments keeps buffer pointers fixed and eliminates fragmentation.

doc_sys_test_004.title: Why LoRA Matrix B Must Be Initialized to Zero
doc_sys_test_004.text: If LoRA matrix B were initialized with random weights along with matrix A, the product B * A would be non-zero at step 0. This would inject random noise into the pretrained weights, immediately destroying the model's pretrained capabilities and causing a massive loss spike on the first training iteration. Initializing B to zero ensures Delta_W starts at strictly zero.

doc_sys_test_005.title: Memory Savings Ratio of Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
doc_sys_test_005.text: In a model with 32 query heads and 8 key/value heads, Grouped-Query Attention reduces KV cache storage and memory bandwidth demand by a factor of 4x (32 / 8) compared to Multi-Head Attention. This allows 4x larger batch sizes or 4x longer context windows to fit within the same physical GPU VRAM capacity during inference.
